title: ROW / ROW — House Desk 002
dek: Sorority Row on the architect’s table: SEC versus Big Ten, national versus local, public history, unequal space, and three playbooks for 2030
body:
A Greek house is never only a house. It is a recruitment machine, an alumni archive, a dining system, a game-day gate, and a public statement about who the campus expects to be visible.

ROW / ROW is PointCast College Football's second House Desk feature. It places Sorority Row on an architect's table, staging an editorial SEC–Big Ten matchup through climate, thresholds, procession, winter shelter, capital, and council visibility. The comparison uses selected official school snapshots, not a normalized conference census.

The field report follows the public lineage from Phi Beta Kappa's 1776 debating society through the early social fraternity, women's societies and Greek-letter organizations, the founding of the National Pan-Hellenic Council at Howard in 1930, and the 2024 Stop Campus Hazing Act. It distinguishes inter/national chapters from campus-specific local organizations and proposes a federated model that keeps local identity while sharing professional risk infrastructure.

Three playbooks move from now to 2030: The Open Ledger makes cost, time, housing, status, accessibility, and safety legible before commitment; The Commons Compact makes prime square footage useful beyond the chapter and creates capital parity for underhoused councils; The Local Face / National Back Office gives small and local organizations access to insurance, training, repair, crisis support, and audit without erasing their history.

Eight selected Midjourney V8.1 plates are imagined editorial architecture scenes, not documentary photographs. The JSON edition carries every job ID, image index, prompt summary, source record, date boundary, and editorial flag.
